title: Canonical way to use webpack to bundle assets AND generate Typescript definitions
body_excerpt: I have a project that builds a typescript library with various assets. Here's how its webpack is configured: [CODE] That works fine. It transforms the assets, complies the Typescript, and bundles it all. But it doesn't generate [code] files, which are needed by any Typescript consumers of the library. Here's what my research has shown: The [code] package recommends using a DeclarationBunderPlugin . But this is an experimental project that hasn't been updated in six years. Some other plugins to handle this that don't seem particularly well supported. See dts-bundle referenced in this SO question as well as other plugin code provided in answers to that question. There is also a plugin referenced in this SO question . I've also seen recommendations to just run [code] and copy over the [code] files. See the comments in this SO question , for example. See also this even older SO question . That's fine, but I was a little surprised not to see any tooling to handle this. As far as I can tell, the webpack documentation is silent on this in its typescript section . Is there a recommended/best/canonical approach for this? Is it just some version of 3. above--i.e., generate your [code] files separately and manually add them to your distribution package? I've put together a small example repo that demonstrates the problems with just using [code] or [code] on their own.
